exercises.instruction: Pick the option that means the same as the English.

items.prompt: “You can take the book on condition that you return it tomorrow.”
options: Yarın geri vermen şartıyla kitabı alabilirsin.
Yarın geri verdiğin şartıyla kitabı alabilirsin.
Yarın geri verirsen şartıyla kitabı alabilirsin.
items.explanation: The clause: -mA + owner + şartıyla. -DIğI and -sA don't go here.
Two “me”s: the first is negation. İç-me-me-niz means “that you don't smoke.”
“They” pay, so the owner is -ları: ödemeleri.
şart and koşul are synonyms: şartıyla = koşuluyla.

items.text: Erken gel___ şartıyla seni de götürürüm.
items.translation: I'll take you along on condition that you come early.
items.explanation: “You” come: gel-me-n şartıyla.

items.text: Evcil hayvan besle___ şartıyla daireyi kiralayabilirsiniz.
items.translation: The apartment can be rented provided that you don't keep pets.
items.explanation: You need the “not”: besle-me-me-niz.

items.translation: You can stay provided that you pay on time.
items.explanation: -mA + “your”: öde-me-niz koşuluyla.

items.translation: We agreed on condition that Ali makes the payment.
items.explanation: The owner of the condition is in the genitive: Ali'nin.

items.translation: The cat can stay on condition that it doesn't scratch the rug.
items.explanation: “Not” + -mA + “its”: tırmala-ma-ma-sı.

exercises.instruction: Find the defective word in the clause and replace it.

items.explanation: -DIğI is for takdirde. With şartıyla, use -mA: vermen.
The condition belongs to someone: şart-ı-yla.
The owner of the condition is in the genitive: Ali'nin.

items.prompt: The landlord is against smoking. Find the word that says the opposite.
items.explanation: You need negation right after the root: iç-me-me-niz.

exercises.instruction: Negotiations in the building chat: build the condition from parts and send a reply.
exercises.description: A nonstandard exercise: the form, the “not,” the owner and the connector come together into a reply to the neighbors and the landlord.

items.explanation: “You” return it: -mA + n + şartıyla.
“Not” after the root, the owner is “you” (pl.): iç-me-me-niz.
This is a case, not a requirement: -DIğI takdirde.
The cat is “it”: tırmala-ma-ma-sı.
“I” pay: öde-me-m.

items.prompt: “You can take part provided that you come early.”
items.explanation: -mA + “your” + koşuluyla: gelmeniz koşuluyla.

items.statement: In the word beslememeniz, the first “me” is negation.
items.explanation: Yes: “not” comes right after the root, then -mA.

items.statement: With şartıyla you usually use -DIğI: verdiğin şartıyla.
items.explanation: No: -DIğI is for takdirde. With şartıyla, use -mA: vermen şartıyla.

items.prompt: Which one is conversational, not contract language?
items.explanation: -sA is a plain “if.” People say it, but contracts aren't written that way.

items.prompt: “…provided that I keep the cat on the balcony.”
items.explanation: “I” will keep it: tut-ma-m şartıyla.
